short_description: 100 easy screen-free plays for ages 0–5, sorted by age, each with prep, mess and play-time icons, easier and harder ideas, a talk line and a safety note.
long_description:
A cup, a box, a sock, or nothing at all. 100 Screen-Free Plays gives you a quick play for every age and every moment of an ordinary day, from first smiles to "and then what happened?"

The plays are sorted into four color-coded age bands (0–1, 1–2, 2–3 and 3–5). Each chapter opens with a one-page "at a glance" guide and a play-basket list, and every play shows the age it starts from, in months.

Every play has the same easy parts: what you need, prep, mess and play-time icons, simple steps, a way to make it easier and a way to make it harder, a "talk while you play" line and a safety note. 89 of the 100 plays need nothing to buy; the pantry list shows what to gather.

You'll also find a Safety first page, a Quick finder for bath time, rainy days, kitchen time, car rides and wind-down, 12 tired-grown-up plays you can do from the couch, a sample screen-free day, and friendly, guilt-free ideas for when screens are on anyway. Every play follows our published safety rules.

The PDF comes in Color and Low-ink files, US Letter and A4, with planners you can type into in free Adobe Acrobat Reader: 100 plays for about 10¢ each. The paperback has a black-and-white interior, with free full-color play pages through the link inside.

Parent education, not medical advice.
